page: The Microsoft Azure F32amds_v7 is a compute and memory-focused virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is built on an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. It provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs with a one-to-one thread-to-core mapping. Hardware instruction support includes AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, AVX-VNNI, AES, and SHA extensions. The processor features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache.

Resource allocation includes 256.0 GB of system memory, delivering an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of a 3780 GB NVMe solid-state drive, supporting low-latency local disk operations alongside standard Azure premium storage options. The instance does not include a GPU accelerator or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark testing demonstrates high compute and memory throughput. Single-core processing in stress-ng ranks in the top ten percent, complemented by top-tier performance in single-threaded compression tests such as gzip and bzip3. Database operations in PassMark achieved top-tier ratings, supported by uncached read memory bandwidth of 216.92 GB/s and write bandwidth of 129.17 GB/s. For CPU-based machine learning inference, small 135M parameter models execute in the top tier, whereas large 70B parameter models drop to average performance tiers.

The F32amds_v7 delivers high efficiency for workloads requiring dedicated physical execution cores, large memory allocations, and fast temporary scratch space. Ideal workloads include in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, high-throughput static web serving, ETL pipelines, and compute-intensive compilation jobs.
description: The Microsoft Azure F32amds_v7 is an enterprise virtual instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, powered by a 32-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz. Built with a dedicated 1:1 thread-to-core ratio, it delivers 32 vCPUs backed by 256.0 GB of memory and 3780 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. The platform integrates AVX-512 and AVX-VNNI instruction sets, achieving top-tier single-core computation, data compression rates, and database transaction throughput in synthetic benchmarks. Memory bandwidth reaches 216.92 GB/s for large uncached reads, effectively supporting heavy data structures. With 8.0 GB of memory per core and no bundled GPU, the F32amds_v7 functions effectively for memory-heavy databases, Redis caches, high-concurrency web tiers, and data transformation pipelines.
